body:
## Summary

For a `showcase` diagram, `validate` and `visual-check` enforce constraints that pull in opposite directions on `meta.viewBox` height, and neither reports the range that satisfies both. An author (human or agent) can only find it by trial and error.

## What happens

On one lifecycle diagram (11 states, 11 transitions, 3 cards), sweeping only the viewBox height at a fixed width of 1075:

| viewBox | `validate` | `visual-check` containment @1440x900 |
|---|---|---|
| 1075x580 | fail - `State "..." exceeds the vertical lifecycle area` | - |
| 1075x585 | ok | pass (scrollHeight 900) |
| 1075x600 | ok | pass (scrollHeight 900) |
| 1075x605 | ok | **fail** (scrollHeight 904) |
| 1075x630 | ok | **fail** (scrollHeight 926) |

The feasible band is roughly **583-600, about 17px**.

The failure messages point in opposite directions:

- `validate` says: `adjust yOffset or increase meta.viewBox[1]`
- `visual-check` then says: `contain the rendered layout within 1440x900, then rerun visual-check`

Following the first message directly causes the second failure. Nothing tells the author that the usable window is ~17px wide, or where it is.

## Widening is not an escape hatch

Trading height for width fails a third check. Same spec, height fixed at 630:

| viewBox | result |
|---|---|
| 1200x630 | fail - `composition/desktop-readability` |
| 1400x700 | fail - same |
| 1600x800 | fail - same |

So the author is boxed in on three sides with no visibility into any of the bounds.

## Why this matters in practice

We drive archify from a non-interactive agent. On one diagram it called `validate` 29 times across 98 turns, oscillating between these constraints, before being cut off by an unrelated quota limit. Diagnostic codes recurred rather than converging (`composition/label-route-clearance` 66 times, `clean-flow/edge-through-node` 33 times). A human hits the same wall more slowly.

We worked around it with an external wrapper that binary-searches the height: probe `validate` to find the floor, then `deliver` + `visual-check` to find the ceiling. It resolves in ~19 probes / under a minute, versus dozens of authoring rounds.

## Suggestions

Any one of these would remove the guesswork:

1. **Report the feasible band.** When `validate` fails on vertical extent, include the height at which containment would start failing - the two checks together already know both bounds.
2. **A `fit` subcommand.** Search the viewBox that satisfies layout, containment and readability, and report the band plus the binding constraint. This is the piece we ended up building outside the tool.
3. **Make the conflict explicit in diagnostics.** When `validate`'s suggested fix (increase viewBox height) would break containment, say so in that message rather than letting the author discover it one command later.

(3) alone would help a lot, since the current wording actively recommends the move that fails next.

## Version

archify 2.17.0-dev.1, `showcase` quality profile, Chromium via ARCHIFY_CHROME.

comments.body:
The height sweep is useful. Telling an agent to increase the viewBox, then rejecting the result for being too tall, is a bad repair loop.

I'd start with your third suggestion: make that conflict explicit and give the author a next step that accounts for readability as well as containment. I wouldn't promise an exact feasible band from static validation alone, since the cards and browser layout also affect it. Could you share the redacted lifecycle JSON used for this sweep? I'd like to keep it as a regression case.

This is related to #356, #358 and #214. The Workflow canvas work in #477 doesn't cover your Lifecycle case, so I'm keeping this open separately.

I'd like to take the current-version reproduction and diagnostic-guidance slice here, starting with the maintainer's suggestion to make conflicting repair advice explicit.

I'll check current dev's Lifecycle behavior, distinguish the older report from the current schema-v3 automatic layout and Reader, and compare validation advice with actual browser containment/readability on valid current inputs. The initial deliverable will be receipts, browser measurements and a status report, followed by a minimal diagnostic or guidance proposal only if a gap remains. The old authored-viewBox height sweep will be treated as historical evidence, not transplanted into an incompatible schema. If the old failure no longer applies, I'll report that rather than manufacture a regression.

I won't infer an exact browser-feasible range from static validation or duplicate the informational projection work in #358 / #569 or the general documentation work in #356 / #804. The original redacted Lifecycle JSON remains useful for historical comparison; any constructed fixture will be identified separately. This work will be AI-assisted, and implementation will follow the resulting scope discussion.

Current-version verification update: **at `dev@6ca6a5c84439b57ea22e0630fe306e1d91587a6e`, I did not reproduce the old validate → increase height → visual-check failure loop in the public/synthetic cases below.** The old Lifecycle authored-geometry path has been replaced: v3 rejects `meta.viewBox` and state `yOffset` with `schema/additionalProperties`. #738 introduced the replacement, and #485 explicitly records that its Lifecycle work was superseded by v3.

The original private 11-state JSON is still unavailable, so this is **not a replay of the original case**. I tested the unchanged public deployment example, a two-state minimum, a synthetic 11-state/11-transition/3-card cycle and its no-card ablation, plus a separate tall 11-state chain. All five pass `validate → deliver → visual-check --require-provenance` at `showcase`, with **30 viewport/theme observations** passing the automated gates. Two retired-field probes and an all-11-states-on-mainPath probe fail as expected; their diagnostics are preserved.

At 1440×900, light / Still / default read view:

| Case | Raw document height | Receipt height | Actual minimum primary / context text |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Public deployment, 3 cards | 1163px | 900px | 12.579 / 9.434px |
| Synthetic 11-state cycle, 3 cards | 1171px | 900px | 14.035 / 10.526px |
| Same cycle, cards removed | 1060px | 900px | 14.035 / 10.526px |
| Tall synthetic chain, no cards | 1409px | 1193px | 8.006 / 6.005px |

Two distinctions matter:

- Current receipt `scrollHeight` subtracts the bottom notes/index rail; it is **not raw DOM document height**. Removing the three cards changed neither the cycle's automatic 1132×638 viewBox, its rendered width nor its text sizes. The cards remain reachable by normal document scrolling.
- The tall control explicitly receives `verticalScrollAccepted: true`. Its ~6px context text meets the machine floor, but the screenshot remains a small-text case, **not evidence of comfortable human reading**. No human or screen-reader acceptance is claimed; `visualReview` remains `pending`.

The current width diagnostic also converged in one controlled probe: putting all 11 synthetic states on mainPath reports `lifecycle/too-wide` (2452px vs a 1395px budget). Moving only this scenario's secondary phases off mainPath preserves all states/transitions/cards and passes the browser checks. This is a constructed recovery example, not a measured real-agent improvement.

**Screenshots** (native 1440×900, DPR 1; public example uses Signal Flow, synthetic examples use Classic):

![Public deployment example on the tested dev](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/testikun/archify/ae4b3aaa4e7d574dc884a854416da630cfa5fe54/docs/issue-468-investigation-20261028/runs/baseline/browser/public-deployment/public-deployment.visual-check.1440x900.light.png)

<details>
<summary>Synthetic 11-state diagram, reachable cards, and tall small-text control</summary>

![Synthetic 11-state first screen](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/testikun/archify/ae4b3aaa4e7d574dc884a854416da630cfa5fe54/docs/issue-468-investigation-20261028/runs/baseline/browser/synthetic-11-cards/synthetic-11-cards.visual-check.1440x900.light.png)

![Same diagram scrolled to its three cards and node index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/testikun/archify/ae4b3aaa4e7d574dc884a854416da630cfa5fe54/docs/issue-468-investigation-20261028/runs/baseline/supplement/synthetic-11-cards.1440x900.bottom.png)

![Tall synthetic control passes the machine floor but has small text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/testikun/archify/ae4b3aaa4e7d574dc884a854416da630cfa5fe54/docs/issue-468-investigation-20261028/runs/tall-no-cards/browser/synthetic-tall/synthetic-tall.visual-check.1440x900.light.png)

</details>

[Pinned evidence: inputs, HTML, all core screenshots, receipts, DOM measurements, reproduction scripts, exact source SHA and limitations](https://github.com/testikun/archify/blob/ae4b3aaa4e7d574dc884a854416da630cfa5fe54/docs/issue-468-investigation-20261028/README.md).

Environment: Node 20.20.2, macOS arm64, Chrome 156.0.8078.48. Light: 1440×900, 1600×1000, 1920×1080, 2048×1320; dark: first/last viewport. Supplemental DOM and text-transform checks used 1440×900 and 1920×1080. AI disclosure: Codex performed the investigation, browser checks, representative screenshot inspection and drafting under **@testikun**'s direction. This is Agent-operated evidence, not full CI or human acceptance.

My conclusion for this slice is to report the superseded path and these current results, without adding a fit command, changing gates, or duplicating #358/#569 or #356/#804. A real current v3 input that still produces a contradictory repair would be useful before designing a remaining fix; I am leaving the issue's acceptance/closure decision to the maintainer.

title: validate and visual-check give opposite guidance on viewBox height, with no way to learn the feasible band
